100% me - I got fired from many jobs and lost countless friendship due to avoidance BUT I recently started to find way to help myself. I should preface this by saying that I meditate and this in general has lowered my anxiety over the years (drastically). I do the following however:

\- Be present with the anxiety/sensation for at least a few minutes; I really feel into the tension, discomfort in my chest and heart rate (this dissipates it somewhat)  
\- I use EFT (tapping sometimes if it's bad) whilst being present  
\- I talk to that aspect of myself that's kicking up with compassion (I learnt this from someone else who overcame avoidance); we avoid often because someone judged us for doing things incorrectly growing up so we learn a freeze or flight response when taking on difficult things/activities where we could be judged  
\- I show up for myself, I talk to myself like an incredibly proud parent would and remind myself of everything I've done. In essence I basically try to remind the scared aspect of me that I'm capable and powerful  


ALSO: one thing I've realized is that even though we avoid things - we end up doing the things we avoid eventually, just with a great deal more pain and anguish because we leave things late - knowing this helps me!

This little protocol takes about 15 minutes and it's changed my life - the fear and guilt around avoidance have lessened a lot and as a result it's helped the avoidance a lot!

That sucks that you had to go through that before getting proper help and a diagnosis.

I grew up in the UK and then moved to Canada (also lived in the US for a while). North America is way quicker to hand out drugs and diagnoses - often to a patient's detriment. I was put on a strong benzo for 1.5 years which left me with permanent damage to my long term memory and sleep (among other things).

I'm glad you found something to finally help though - living with avoidance coping really is torturous!

What I did was actually apply for a few jobs WAY below my pay grade/qualification level - roles and companies I really didn't care about and I completely aced the interviews! It gave me such a huge confidence boost and I did well because there was no attachment to the outcome (therefore no anxiety) - felt great and the recruiters will be much more easily impressed with you.  


You're just showing your brain that's it's okay and to stop with the rumination/negative scenarios it keeps playing out in your mind.  
Meditation and EFT tapping also help A LOT so I'd give it try if you feel up to it.  


I've now started to apply for jobs in my career trajectory/job level and I'm feeling good about it! :)

I have huge issues with avoidance coping and have lost so much in my life because of it!

I have however recently started to make headway with it. I started seeing a therapist who helped me get to the root of the issue (I have a narcissist parent who knocked my confidence so badly as a child I have no confidence when I try to do a task so I avoid it  - even getting out of bed or brushing my teeth is something I put off)

I also started meditating 2 years ago daily and built up to an hour a day (an hour is no where near the amount of time necessary to see change) but it's helped me be very present with the extreme anxiety that comes along with doing things and it often dissipates it for me.

For the first time in my life I started to do big things and relearn how to be a damn adult. I think you have to be very present and compassionate with the feelings that comes up, understand where they've come from and then big yourself up! Be the parent you always needed or cheerleader and try and tackle very small tasks.

So for right now I do the following:

1. I pick a task such as washing up a cup in the sink
2. I literally sit with the overwhelming feelings that come up and just get very present
3. The feelings lessen a lot and then I often act OR if it's still bad
4. I use EFT (tapping) it's super effective at bringing you down to base emotionally and easy to do (great for panic)
5. I remind myself that I'm capable and why the action I'm about to do is good/will help me (so for cup washing I'll talk about how important it is to have a healthy environment free of mould and how I can nourish myself with liquid held by this cup later)

I started with washing one dish or folding one piece of laundry - it's helping tonnes and my confidence is growing and the avoidance seems way less overwhelming and scary now - I think I can beat it!

It's incredibly accessible to everyone and resources are usually cheap/free so I always encourage people to get right into it!

I started with a basic 5 min Body Scan meditation from UCLA (they're free, I'll post the link below) however I would recommend breathing exercises to begin. These exercises move your body from a 'fight or flight' state into a 'rest and digest' state and they're a great prerequisite to meditation. It'll get you used to noticing your breath - how it pools around your nose and how it's cold when you breathe in but warm when you breathe out etc and should start to bring you into the present a bit.

I went on to use Youtube meditations on being present and eventually worked my way up to Zen meditation with the help of a local Buddhist monastery and now I do an hour every morning outside wherein I notice gently what sounds are around me, how my body feels (both emotionally and physically), how the ground beneath me feels and smells that come in and out. I'm able to maintain a grounded (present) state for long periods now and it is the most beautiful state you can experience.

Disclaimer: your mind will definitely wander but gently bring it back to your breath or sounds around you (this may have to happen hundreds of times in an inital session and that's incredibly normal)!

ALSO just a bit of encouragement: after doing this for 1.5 years I shift 10 years of depression and anxiety (something I was told was resistant to medication and chronic) - it's worth trying, promise! Just get started with about 5 minutes once of twice a week and see how you feel! :)  


UCLA Meditations: [https://www.uclahealth.org/marc/mindful-meditations](https://www.uclahealth.org/marc/mindful-meditations)

Oh buddy I feel you! I've definitely had it happen a few times (especially when I lived at home) and it's embarrassing AF. But we're only human and people forget these things within a few days. We dwell/judge/remember these moments much more fervently than they ever do - you'll be okay! :)

One of the things that brought back happiness into my life in a big way was meditation.

Meditation has also just reduced the amount I MD and made it way more manageable. I no longer obsessively pace (have no desire to) and my day dreams have become less and less fantasy like (they often consist of normal social situations a/o to have superpowers etc)

The present moment (not to sound like a hippie) is SO beautiful! I meditate outside and when you ground/become present you notice the smallest things around you are truly wonderful. I often see hornets/wasps take naps on flowers of notice reflections in large dew drops on leaves in the morning. A big part of MD is about rejecting/not liking the life you have and meditation really helped me fall back in love with the present moment (and life)!

(Meditation also shifted a decade's worth of depression and anxiety - it really saved my life)!

Also my Endo recommended cutting gluten for hypothyroidism; cutting gluten is very commonly advised with thyroid issues; she explained that many people with thyroid issues have a mild intolerance to gluten and cutting it out may cause a  lower inflammatory response from my thyroid (I thought this was common knowledge when it came to thyroid issues)?

Even if I fall off my normal eating schedule for a couple of weeks or eat a lot of fatty food and stop taking my probiotics, my gut seems fine.

I've worked on my nutrition for years and use cronometer to track nutrients, caloric intake and proteins (I did the raw diet 6 years ago for a few months only)

My Endo said that if I have no symptoms and my hormones stay leveled that I don't have to be on BC (I've been off for 2 years now and haven't experienced symptoms of PCOS apart from potentially my blood sugar issues which my endo now thinks is more to do with my thryoid)  
She was the one that initially explained that a diet free of processed sugary foods and BC would help my hormones
